introduction: Short of money in Windsor, Sir John Falstaff decides that two married women offer an easy route to their husbands' wealth. His identical love letters give Mistress Ford and Mistress Page an opportunity to answer him together. Their intended revenge becomes entangled with Ford's jealousy, a quarrel between a Welsh parson and a French doctor, and competing plans for Anne Page's marriage. As messages, disguises and false assurances circulate through the town, the people who expect to direct others repeatedly misunderstand what is happening.

fullSynopsis.text: Falstaff needs money and imagines that Mistress Ford and Mistress Page welcome his attentions. He sends both essentially the same love letter, hoping to gain access to their husbands' purses. His dismissed followers Pistol and Nym warn the husbands. Page trusts his wife, but Ford becomes suspicious. The women compare the letters, recognize Falstaff's presumption and resolve to encourage him only to punish him. Meanwhile, Shallow and the Welsh parson Evans promote Slender as a husband for Anne Page. Doctor Caius also wants Anne and challenges Evans for supporting a rival. Quickly, Caius's servant, encourages several suitors with contradictory assurances.

Quickly carries the wives' invitation to Falstaff, pretending that they desire him. Ford approaches Falstaff disguised as a wealthy gentleman called Brook. He offers money if Falstaff will seduce Mistress Ford, inventing a story that her fall would help Brook win her himself. Falstaff takes the money, announces his appointment with her and insults Ford to his face without recognizing him. Ford treats this as proof of his wife's guilt. Elsewhere, the Host has sent Caius and Evans to different places for their duel. When they discover his trick, the two men abandon their quarrel and agree to seek revenge on him.

At Ford's house, the wives prepare a large laundry basket. Falstaff begins his courtship, but Mistress Page interrupts with a warning that Ford is coming to search the house. The women hide Falstaff under dirty linen and have servants carry him away. Ford arrives with neighbours, misses the concealed knight and finds nobody during his search. Falstaff later describes being tipped into the Thames. Quickly nevertheless persuades him to accept another appointment. When he tells Brook how he escaped and where he is going next, Ford's jealousy revives. His renewed determination to catch Falstaff sets up a second search.

Anne, meanwhile, rejects the husbands her parents favour: Page supports Slender, and Mistress Page prefers Caius. Fenton admits that her wealth first attracted him but declares that he now loves her herself. Anne returns his affection. At the next meeting with Mistress Ford, Falstaff refuses another escape in the basket. The wives dress him as an old woman whom Ford dislikes and calls a witch. Ford empties the basket, then beats the disguised Falstaff out of the house. The women finally disclose their scheme to their husbands. Ford asks forgiveness, and they plan a public humiliation at Herne's oak.

The Host suffers a separate trick: supposed Germans borrow three horses and ride away with them. Evans and Caius arrive with warnings about impostors and the nonexistent visiting duke. For the final joke against Falstaff, the townspeople prepare children and others as fairies. Both Pages use the occasion to arrange Anne's secret marriage, each believing that a particular costume will identify her to the preferred suitor. Anne instead plans to leave with Fenton. He recruits the Host to arrange a priest. Falstaff, still convinced that the wives want him, agrees to meet them wearing horns as Herne the hunter.

In the park the supposed fairies surround Falstaff, burn his fingers and pinch him while singing against lust. He believes them supernatural until the neighbours reveal the deception. Ford identifies himself as Brook, demands his money back and acknowledges his wife's honesty. Slender and Caius discover that each has taken away a disguised boy rather than Anne; Caius says he has married his. Anne returns with Fenton, who announces their binding marriage and defends her escape from a loveless match. Her parents accept the result and wish them joy. Mistress Page invites everyone, including the chastened Falstaff, home to laugh over the night together.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Falstaff's quarrel with Shallow and Slender introduces a town full of grievances, matchmaking and competing accounts of wrongdoing. Evans proposes that Slender marry Anne Page and sends Simple to ask Quickly's help. Falstaff, pressed for money, dismisses Pistol and Nym when they refuse to carry his love letters to Mistress Ford and Mistress Page. He means to profit from the women's access to their husbands' money, while his former servants plan to expose him. At Caius's house, the doctor discovers Simple's errand and challenges Evans for promoting Slender. Quickly promises to support Caius, then gives Fenton encouragement as well. Her conflicting assurances establish how unreliable the suitors' information about Anne can be.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Mistress Page and Mistress Ford discover their identical letters and agree to lure Falstaff into humiliating situations while protecting their honesty. Pistol warns Ford and Nym warns Page. Page dismisses their accusations; Ford decides to investigate in disguise. Quickly tells Falstaff that both women desire him and arranges a visit to Mistress Ford. Calling himself Brook, Ford offers Falstaff money to compromise his own wife, supposedly so that Brook can then win her. Falstaff accepts and reveals the appointment, making Ford mistake the wives' trap for an adulterous arrangement. The Host also organizes a different deception: Caius waits to duel Evans at a place where Evans has not been sent. The Host promises to help Caius's courtship instead.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Evans anxiously sings while waiting for the duel. The Host reunites the opponents and reveals that he deliberately separated them; Caius and Evans agree to turn their anger against him. Ford gathers neighbours for a search of his house. The wives, anticipating the intrusion, conceal Falstaff in a basket of dirty washing and have him carried away before Ford can find him. Their joke ends with Falstaff being thrown into the Thames, as he later recounts. Anne and Fenton affirm their attachment despite her parents' preferences for Slender and Caius. Quickly brings Falstaff a fresh invitation, and he tells Brook about both the basket and the next visit. Ford again resolves to expose the supposed affair.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Evans tests young William Page's Latin while Quickly repeatedly mistakes his terms for indecencies. At Ford's house, Falstaff's second visit ends with another warning of a search. Refusing the basket, he accepts disguise as an old woman from Brentford. Ford searches the linen and beats the disguised knight away without recognizing him. The wives now explain their tricks, bringing Ford to repent his jealousy. The couples devise a final meeting at Herne's oak, with Falstaff horned and children dressed as fairies. Meanwhile impostors steal the Host's horses. Each Page secretly directs Anne toward a different husband during the entertainment, but Anne and Fenton arrange their own escape and enlist the Host to provide a priest.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Falstaff prepares for the midnight meeting, still boasting to Brook that he will deliver Mistress Ford to him. Page and Mistress Page separately instruct Anne's unwanted suitors, while Evans organizes the disguised fairies. At the oak, the wives draw Falstaff into the performance. Quickly, Evans, Pistol and the children impersonate supernatural beings, testing his chastity with candle flames, then singing and pinching him. The neighbours reveal themselves and expose his folly; Ford reveals Brook's identity and renounces his jealousy. Slender and Caius have each carried off a boy in costume. Anne and Fenton return married, defeating both parental schemes. The Pages accept their daughter's choice, and the company invites Falstaff to join their celebration at home.
